title: Point-Focused Attention Meets Context-Scan State Space: Robust Biological Visual Perception for Point Cloud Representation
claim: Prior perception modes capture only local detail or only coarse global context; ours mimics foveal vision by combining a sharp focus with blurred context.
layout: 5 panels in a row, left-to-right, red focus dot and orange circle
description: A single row of five panels shows the same cartoon panda image, with captions (a) to (e) underneath. (a) is the noisy, speckled point-cloud-like panda, sharp everywhere. (b) is foveal vision. It is sharp and clear around a red dot on the panda's eye and progressively blurred toward the periphery. (c) is point-focused attention, the proposed method. It has the same blurred periphery, plus an orange circle around the red dot that shows a sharp, noisy local region. This closely matches (b). (d) is local neighbor attention. The surroundings are almost black, with only the orange-circled local region visible. (e) is spatial downsampling attention. The whole image is blurred and has no sharp focus region, though the red dot is still marked. The eye goes first to the red dot and orange circle, then compares the panels.
caption: A comparison of different information perception ways, where the red dot indicates the visual focus and the orange circle denotes the local awareness range. Our point-focused attention aligns more closely with natural foveal vision than the perceptual modes in (d) and (e).
abstract: Synergistically capturing intricate local structures and global contextual dependencies has become a critical challenge in point cloud representation learning. To address this, we introduce PointLearner, a point cloud representation learning network that closely aligns with biological vision which employs an active, foveation-inspired processing strategy, thus enabling local geometric modeling and long-range dependency interactions simultaneously. Specifically, we first design a point-focused attention, which simulates foveal vision at the visual focus through a competitive normalized attention mechanism between local neighbors and spatially downsampled features. The spatially downsampled features are extracted by a pooling method based on learnable inducing points, which can flexibly adapt to the non-uniform distribution of point clouds as the number of inducing points is controlled and they interact directly with point clouds. Second, we propose a context-scan state space that mimics eye's saccade inference, which infers the overall semantic structure and spatial content in the scene through a scan path guided by the Hilbert curve for the bidirectional S6. With this focus-then-context biomimetic design, PointLearner demonstrates remarkable robustness and achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple point cloud tasks.
